title: Scott K. Fish: Brian Holland: Motown's Drummers Were Unbeatable (phone interview, 12 May 1982; posted 7 September 2015)
notes: Holland, producer of Holland-Dozier-Holland's records: "Pistol came in after Benny." "He was more of a shuffle kind of a drummer. He was the best at the shuffles." "On the shuffle things, like Heat Wave, I know Pistol played on that. He might have played on Baby Love by the Supremes." Benny Benjamin "had to play at least 75-percent" of the Four Tops' and Supremes' records. "A couple of those guys - like Benny and Pistol - always was emotionally into it." Allen played at the 20 Grand, a Detroit bar.

title: Where Did Our Love Go - Wikipedia
notes: The Supremes, June 1964, Holland-Dozier-Holland; their first number one. Personnel: "Drums by Richard 'Pistol' Allen"; Mike Valvano stomping on boards.

title: Reach Out I'll Be There - Wikipedia
notes: The Four Tops, August 1966, Holland-Dozier-Holland; number one in the US and the UK. Names no drummer. The arranger Paul Riser overdubbed a piccolo and flute in the intro and "a drum pattern played with timpani mallets on a tambourine head".

title: Richard "Pistol" Allen at the kit (Metro Times photograph, on Wikipedia as File:Richard Pistol Allen.jpg)
notes: Black and white, outdoors, undated (the clothes say late 1960s or early 1970s): a cowboy hat, tinted glasses, a dark shirt printed with pale flowers, open at the neck, a thin chain, a dark sleeveless vest, a bracelet; a silver sparkle Ludwig kit.

title: Drummerszone: Richard "Pistol" Allen
notes: Primary session drummer for the Funk Brothers; a studio set of Ludwig, Slingerland, Rogers and Gretsch parts; influences Max Roach, Buddy Rich and Benny Benjamin; names Heat Wave, The Way You Do the Things You Do and Reach Out I'll Be There.
